title: I am as My servant thinks
word: I am as My servant thinks
hookLine: Allah says, I am as My servant thinks of Me (Bukhari)

cards: Two people get the same voicemail from a doctor's office: please call us back. One spends the afternoon sure it's bad news, rehearsing every outcome. The other assumes it's about rescheduling, and makes lunch.
Same message. Two very different afternoons. What a person expects shapes the day they live.
Today, one of the sacred hadith, and it's about expecting. Its word is a whole sentence: I am as My servant thinks.

teach.h: I AM AS MY SERVANT THINKS OF ME.
teach.b: First, the line. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ relates that Allah says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. It's short, and it says a great deal.
In this report, Allah ties the way He meets a person to what that person expects of Him. Second, the name for it.

teach.h: THINKING WELL OF ALLAH, TO THE END.
teach.b: Scholars call this husn al-zann billah, thinking well of Allah: expecting mercy, forgiveness, an answer. It isn't only for easy days.
In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet tells his companions that none of them should die except while thinking well of Allah. So this expectation is meant to last to the very end. Third, the balance.
Commentators on this hadith add a careful note: thinking well of Allah isn't the same as assuming nothing matters.
They pair hope with effort. A person thinks well of Allah while praying, while repenting, while trying. A student who studies and hopes for a good grade is thinking well.
A student who skips every class and hopes is only guessing. Fourth, the next lines.
The same report goes on: if he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself, and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it.
Remembering runs both ways. After that, the report keeps going, into a picture of distance and of speed. That picture is tomorrow's.

how: Muslims may recall this hadith in times of worry or illness, and scholars teach thinking well of Allah as hope joined to prayer, repentance and effort.

games.q: what does “i am as my servant thinks” mean?
o: a servant should think of his master all day long
Allah judges people by their thoughts, never their deeds
Allah meets a person as that person expects of Him

games.q: I am as My servant thinks — tap the pairs.
p: I am as My servant thinks of Me

s: the hadith means Allah becomes whatever a person imagines
commentators pair it with effort: thinking well of Allah while praying, repenting and trying.
the same report says Allah remembers the one who remembers Him
within himself, or in a gathering, and Allah remembers him in a better one.
thinking well of Allah is only for good days
in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet says none should die except while thinking well of Allah.

games.q: a friend says: 'if Allah is as I think, I'll just assume He's fine with whatever I do.' what do the commentators on this hadith say?
o: thinking well of Allah goes with prayer, repentance and effort.
you should never hope for anything.
games.why: hope walks with effort. the student who studies and hopes is thinking well; the one who skips class and hopes is guessing.

practice: Bring to mind one thing that's worrying you, hold it gently, and notice what you've been expecting about it, maybe the worst, maybe nothing at all.

Without pretending the worry isn't real, try the other way of expecting: if you believe, meet it expecting Allah's mercy; if you're not sure what you believe, simply expect that some good can still come of it.
Breathe in on the worry, breathe out on the better expectation, and don't force anything.

wordCard.voice: I am as My servant thinks. A sacred hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari: Allah meets a person as that person expects of Him. Today's word.
